title: Moving Stones Until Consecutive II
summary: Given an integer array representing the positions of stones on the X-axis, determine the minimum and maximum number of moves required to arrange the stones in three consecutive positions.
statement: Given an integer array representing the positions of stones on the X-axis, determine the minimum and maximum number of moves required to arrange the stones in three consecutive positions. An endpoint stone (one with the smallest or largest position) can only be moved to a position that is not an endpoint. The game ends when no more moves are possible. Return an array where the first element is the minimum number of moves and the second element is the maximum number of moves.
constraints: At least three distinct stone positions are provided.
An endpoint move must place it strictly inside the remaining range and not leave it an endpoint.
hints: Maximum moves consume interior holes after choosing which endpoint gap to abandon.
Minimum moves maximize stones already fitting in an interval of width n using a sliding window.
Use n-window count, with the n-1 tightly packed special case requiring two moves.
Every normal missing spot can be filled by one endpoint move; the special rule prevents the apparent one-move finish.
editorial: Every normal missing spot can be filled by one endpoint move; the special rule prevents the apparent one-move finish.

tests.explanation: Sorted positions 4,7,9 need one minimum move and allow two maximum moves.
The special near-consecutive arrangement requires two minimum moves.
